input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: research programme sensing-selfcal (pick_track draw 0.992): milestone 4g, score the f-alone update test on every disjoint split from milestone 4f's stored solves, test a robust (MAD) jackknife, fold milestones 4f and 4g into the paper draft
errors: First run of analyse.py returned NaN for the pre-registered leave-one-view-out ranges at k = 6: every 7 + 6 split uses all 13 views, so dropping a view leaves no split. Reported as undefined, with the k = 5 ranges added and labelled as added after the first run.
integrity_issues: Milestone 4g corrects a published headline: milestone 4d's (and the paper draft's) 61% power for the borrowed-threshold f-alone test came from 60 splits and a 99th percentile of 180 statistics; on every split it is 43%. Corrected in the paper, the project README (with a pointer at the 4d headline), project.json and the post; the old figure is reproduced exactly (61.25%) on the old splits, so it was not a code error.

doc_friction.issue: Says to run `pyenv.py pytest numpy matplotlib` for project tests, but sensing-selfcal's tests import cv2; the first pytest run failed at collection until opencv-python-headless was added (pyenv maps it to cv2 correctly). The project's requirements.txt route (`pytest -r <project>/requirements.txt`) would have avoided it; the short form is what a run reaches for first.
Default markers are DONE or EXIT; my log ended with 'exit 0' (lowercase), so it waited the full timeout although the job had finished. Minor; the help text is accurate.

deviations.why: The output standards ask to compare against the strongest published methods; this milestone compares only variants of the programme's own test (plain jackknife, borrowed threshold, robust jackknife), because the question was internal (does the 4d headline survive every split, and does a robust scale remove the borrowed threshold).
deviations.did: Scored the three variants on every split; external baselines stay with the paper's Section 10 list.
deviations.result: A correction and a better variant landed; external comparison remains open in the paper's to-do list.
